title: Ashura remembered
hookLine: Sunnis fast for Musa's rescue; Shia mourn Husayn; some keep both
last: A NEW CLOTH FOR THE HOUSE.

lines: A CUP OF WATER ON A STREET CORNER.
cards: A folding table on a street corner. A steel cooler, a stack of paper cups, and someone pouring water for every stranger who walks by, no charge.
In some Shia neighborhoods, on the tenth of Muharram, tables like this appear. A few streets away, someone else is fasting, and will break the fast at sunset. Same day, same calendar page.
The cup remembers a thirst on the plain of Karbala. The fast remembers a rescue at the sea. And some people, quietly, keep both.

teach.b: Ashura means the tenth: the tenth day of Muharram, the first month of the year.

teach.h: A FAST FOR MUSA'S RESCUE AT THE SEA.
teach.b: Start with the rescue. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari tells how the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came to Medina and found the Jews there fasting on this day. He asked why.

They said it was the day God saved Musa and his people from Pharaoh, and Musa fasted it in thanks. The Prophet said he had more right to Musa than they, and he fasted it, and told his community to fast.
So the first meaning of the day is gratitude for a sea that opened. Then the grief.

teach.h: MOURNING FOR HUSAYN'S THIRST AT KARBALA.
teach.b: Years after the Prophet's death, on this same tenth, his grandson Husayn was killed at Karbala with his family and companions, cut off from the river, thirsty. We told that day in full earlier this year.
For Shia Muslims, Ashura became the heart of the year's mourning: gatherings, elegies, the story read aloud again. The water tables remember his thirst. Third, the two together.

teach.h: SOME KEEP BOTH ON ONE DAY.
teach.b: Sunni Muslims keep the fast from the Prophet's practice, and they honor Husayn as the Prophet's grandson. Some fast and grieve on the same day. Shia scholars have their own views on fasting that day, and they differ.
Nobody needs to rank the memories to hold them.

teach.h: HOLY DAYS LIVE IN SMALL THINGS.
teach.b: Look back at this stretch, lanterns, a cannon, a drummer, caravans, a new cloth, and now a cup of water: holy days survive in small things people do with their hands.

how: On the tenth of Muharram, Sunni Muslims who keep the day fast, following the Prophet's practice, some adding the ninth; Shia communities hold mourning gatherings for Husayn, recite elegies, and some set up stands giving free water in memory of his thirst.

games.q: you're the Prophet, newly arrived in Medina. you find the Jews of the city fasting on the tenth of Muharram. they tell you it's for Musa's rescue from Pharaoh. what do you do?
o: leave their fast to them; it's their day.
fast it too, and tell your community to fast.
forbid fasting on that day altogether.
games.why: the hadith in Bukhari says he answered that he had more right to Musa than they did, fasted the day, and told his community to fast it.

practice: Fill a glass, or hold your hands as if holding one, and think first of the sea opening for people who were sure they were trapped, then of a camp by a river where the water was kept from them.

Hold the glass a moment without drinking and let rescue and grief both be true, then drink, or breathe, slowly. If you pray, you can say the line the Qur'an gives for loss: we are Allah's, and unto Him we are returning.

wordCard.voice: Ashura remembered. The tenth of Muharram: a fast of thanks for Musa's rescue, and mourning for Husayn's death at Karbala. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the tenth, the tenth day of Muharram.

carryVoice: Your line: rescue and grief. One day can hold both. Tomorrow a new stretch begins: what the history teaches.
